rationale: The staging flag for going live, and nothing more. The worker is contract-locked to production_no_live (mode string, activation file and runtime config all three), so flipping this does not and cannot place an order; it records the operator's intent, the station allowlist the first live batch is limited to, and travels into the go-live migration as its input. The migration that mints the live contract must refuse to run while live_enabled is false.
allowlist_note: The live batch is the bar's complement, not a list. Operator ruling 2026-08-30: station_scope=all_except_barred, so every station the model produces for trades unless it is on live_station_exclusions_v1. station_allowlist is empty on purpose -- it is only read in scope=explicit, and a populated list sitting here in derived mode is exactly the stale-list trap this replaced. The eight-station batch of 2026-08-28 went stale in two days (KLGA and KSFO both reached 5/5 and were absent from it while KORD sat on it with three chains), and the fleet roster moved 45 to 48 in the same window, so any frozen enumeration is wrong by the time it is read. Membership is derived from book history rather than the coordinate roster: LLBG, LTFM and UUWW are on the roster and have never produced a position, and a live batch cannot contain a station the model has never computed. Note the consequence: a newly onboarded station joins the live batch as soon as it books, before the automatic layer has the five settlements it needs to judge it -- bounded by the per-scope stake cap, and the price of a complement-defined batch.
